subject: Recap & next steps — performance SLOs, context window & token limits
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finco.com>, Priya Singh <priya.singh@finco.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Sep 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Recap & next steps — performance SLOs, context window & token limits

Hi Alex & Priya,

Thanks again for the call earlier — good discussion. Quick recap and proposed next steps focused on the Performance/SLO items we talked about: latency targets, throughput/concurrency, streaming requirements, and how context window/token limits affect latency.

Key points from FinCo:
- Desired latency SLOs: p95 <= 300–500ms for single-response interactions (user-facing chat flows). For some batch/analysis jobs higher latency (up to 2s) is acceptable.
- Peak concurrent active users: ~200 concurrent sessions during peak, with steady-state throughput ~40 QPS for chat API.
- Context window: many workflows require including long legal documents — typical context per request ~8k–20k tokens, with occasional up to ~50k tokens for full-file analysis.
- Output size: normally 200–800 tokens; some summarization flows generate up to 4k tokens.
- Streaming: UX requires token-by-token streaming for chat and progressive summarization.

Observations / tradeoffs we discussed:
- Larger context windows (20k+) significantly increase tokenization, KV-cache memory, and initial attention compute — which raises tail latency and reduces throughput.
- Streaming mitigates perceived latency for long outputs but doesn't reduce total compute; per-token latency and network chunking are important.
- For the p95 targets you quoted, we expect to meet them for typical 2k token context + 300–800 token output on a dedicated GPU pool using optimized kernels and quantized models. For 50k context + 4k output we would recommend a dedicated configuration and can expect higher p95s (1s+ in many cases) unless we use model/quantization tradeoffs and aggressive batching.

Proposed next steps (action items):
1) FinCo: share a small representative sample of your typical request payloads (anonymized) — 10–20 examples covering short chat, long-document context, and large summaries. (Priya recommended examples.)
2) Redwood: run targeted benchmarks against those samples (latency p50/p95, throughput at 1x/2x/peak concurrency) and share a short SLO recommendation doc + CSV of results.
3) Redwood: propose two config options — "balanced" (lower-cost, slightly higher latency for huge contexts) and "performance" (dedicated pool, prioritized routing, model variant tuned for low tail latency).
4) Schedule a 45-minute deep-dive demo to walk through the benchmark results and discuss Dedicated sizing/costing — propose Wed or Thu next week.

I'll attach a short SLO checklist and a template for sample payloads.

Thanks,
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Marissa — thanks for the recap, that aligns with our notes. A couple clarifying items before we share the sample payloads:

1) Concurrency vs throughput — when you say "200 concurrent sessions," does Redwood treat that as 200 simultaneous open connections streaming tokens, or 200 active request workers? We need to map to our infra expectations (we have ~60k monthly active users).

2) For the large context case (50k tokens), any quick guidance on whether you recommend chunking + retrieval vs sending the whole file as context for best latency/quality tradeoff?

3) Model variants — do you have a recommended starting point (quantized FP16 vs int8) for the performance config that preserves our summarization quality? If we need to accept slightly lower ROUGE for better p95, what should we expect?

We can get you 15 anonymized payloads by EOD tomorrow. Also please confirm availability for Thu 24 Sep for the deep-dive (late morning PST works for us).

Thanks,
Alex Johnson
Principal Product Manager — AI Platforms
FinCo

Hi all,

Thanks — Marissa, Dylan and I ran the first pass of the benchmarks this morning. High level:
- Short context (<=2k) + 500 token output: p50 ~ 85ms, p95 ~ 240ms on dev Dedicated-like config (quantized int8 model).
- Mid context (10–20k) + 1k output: p50 ~ 220ms, p95 ~ 620ms (streaming enabled reduces perceived latency for end users).
- Long context (~50k) + 3k output: p50 ~ 900ms, p95 ~ 1.6s — this is the costly bucket.

I've uploaded the CSV and a 1-page SLO recommendation to Drive: https://drive.google.com/finco-performance-slo-doc. Also attaching the CSV here.

Attachments:
- finco-latency-benchmark.csv
- redwood-slo-summary.pdf

We recommend starting FinCo on the "Balanced" profile for initial rollout (dedicated pool with autoscale, int8 quantization) and enabling streaming for chat flows. For mission-critical low-latency flows where p95 < 400ms is required even on long contexts, we should discuss a Performance tier with higher-priority routing and a model variant tuned for latency (larger instance count + lower batch windows).

Marissa — I can join Thu morning PST for the deep-dive.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
